key_idea: Only 28 possible jump lengths: try each d from 1 and check that phase((d*i) mod 28) matches the i-th observation.
sketch: Encode the phase table as a function of day mod 28. For d = 1..28 simulate the n jumps starting from day 0 (the first observation is after one jump, i.e. day d) and output the first d consistent with every observation. O(28 n). Pitfalls: the table is asymmetric (Quarter is 5-8 but 20-22, Crescent 1-4 but 23-27), and d=28 is a legal answer (all New).
